description: Delete a problem for good, as the Problems page does. Unlike dismiss_problem, nothing of it remains, not even on its conversation. delete_category also deletes its category and every problem in it; add_to_never_flag writes a do-not-flag rule from the category (or the problem), so the judge stops reporting that behaviour. Prefer dismiss_problem for a false alarm the team may want to see later. Deleting cannot be undone. Before you call this, look the item up so you know it exists; if it does not, say so and ask nothing. Then tell the user plainly what will be deleted, naming it as the lookup shows it, and ask whether they are sure, in words like: "You asked me to delete <what>. Are you sure you want to proceed?" Then stop and wait. Call it only when the user's next message confirms that exact item. If several items could be meant, list them with their ids and ask which; the user's choice is not a confirmation, so name the chosen item with its id and ask again. If they decline, hesitate, ask something else or change the request, do not delete; ask again before deleting later.

add_to_never_flag.description: Also write a do-not-flag rule from the problem's category (or the problem when it has none), so the judge stops reporting it.
add_to_never_flag.title: Add To Never Flag

delete_category.description: Also delete the problem's category and every other problem in it.
delete_category.title: Delete Category

problem.description: The problem's id, as list_problems shows it.
problem.title: Problem

project.description: The project's number (as the app shows it, e.g. 12 or '#12') or its name. Optional when the organization has one project.
project.title: Project
